claim_text: The FBI is investigating an apparent intrusion into its National Crime Information Center (NCIC)
summary: CNN, NBC News, AP and ABC News each report, citing their own unnamed sources, that the FBI is investigating an apparent breach or hack of NCIC.
detail: NBC News (two people briefed), AP (one person familiar with the matter) and ABC News (one law enforcement source, who it says confirmed the database was hacked) each have their own sourcing, separate from CNN's two. Reuters, WUSA9, BleepingComputer and others relay CNN and count with it. None of these sources is named, and the FBI has not confirmed it.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: CNN and NBC News each attribute the investigation to two people briefed; AP attributes it to a person familiar with the matter; ABC News to a law enforcement source. Reuters, WUSA9 and BleepingComputer relay CNN, so they count with CNN.
notes: Relabelled from Reported on Nov 21, 2026: NBC News is a second outlet with its own sources. AP and ABC News added Nov 21 evening. This confirms that an investigation into an apparent breach is under way, not what was reached or who did it.

claim_text: The intrusion was found in recent days, and FBI officials knew of it by Thursday, Nov 19
summary: CNN says the intrusion was discovered 'in recent days' and that bureau officials had learned of it by Thursday, Nov 19.
detail: CNN does not give a discovery date or say when the intrusion began. WUSA9's summary of CNN says officials learned of it on Thursday.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: CNN says 'the discovery of the latest intrusion in recent days' and refers to Thursday, after bureau officials learned of it.

claim_text: The FBI has not commented publicly on the report
summary: The FBI did not respond to CNN, Reuters, BleepingComputer or ABC News, told NBC News it had no comment, and declined to comment to AP. Its press releases page and official X accounts had no NCIC statement as of the evening of Nov 21.
detail: Rechecked about 8:20 PM ET on Nov 21. the President spoke about the reports on Nov 21 (see the claim below), but that is not an FBI statement. An FBI statement would change most of this page.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: CNN, Reuters, BleepingComputer and ABC News each say the FBI did not respond to them, NBC News says the FBI had no comment, and AP says the FBI declined; the FBI press page lists no NCIC statement.

claim_text: What was accessed, how the intruders got in, and who they are
summary: No source says what part of NCIC was reached, how the intruders got in, or who is responsible. No one has claimed it.
detail: CNN calls them 'apparent hackers' and ABC News says the perpetrators and scale are unclear. Naming an attacker needs official or independent sourcing.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: CNN, Reuters and NBC News report only that an investigation exists; ABC News says who did it and how big it is are unclear. NBC says the FBI has not addressed who may have breached the system.

claim_text: Whether any NCIC records were copied or changed
summary: No source says records were copied or changed. A former FBI official told CNN the bigger worry is whether the accuracy of records could be compromised.
detail: The former official was speaking generally about the risk, not reporting a finding.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: CNN quotes the former official's concern about record accuracy but reports no finding on data taken or altered.

claim_text: NCIC is the FBI-run database that criminal justice agencies nationwide use to share records
summary: The FBI says NCIC holds records entered by criminal justice agencies nationwide; as of 2023 it had 22 files, more than 18 million active records and over 100,000 partners.
detail: These are the FBI's own figures, not counts of anything affected.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The FBI's NCIC page gives the 22 files, 18 million-plus active records and 100,000-plus criminal justice partners.

claim_text: Police use NCIC in everyday checks such as traffic stops, and must confirm a hit before acting
summary: The FBI says officers use NCIC to learn instantly whether a driver is wanted or a vehicle stolen, and that a hit must be confirmed before official action.
detail: This is why a former FBI official told CNN record accuracy matters.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The FBI's NCIC page describes traffic-stop use and says agencies must confirm a hit before acting on it.

claim_text: In September, the FBI jobs site was breached; the FBI blamed a contractor's missed security patch
summary: ShinyHunters claimed a breach of FBIJobs.gov in September. In October an FBI cyber official said a contractor failed to apply a security patch, and the FBI removed the contractor.
detail: This is a separate, earlier incident. It is on this page for context because CNN calls the NCIC intrusion the second FBI breach in recent months.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: NBC quotes the FBI's statement on the contractor's missed patch; BleepingComputer and TechCrunch separately report the breach.

claim_text: The NCIC intrusion is the second breach of an FBI system in recent months
summary: CNN and Reuters describe the NCIC intrusion as the second breach of an FBI system in recent months, after the September jobs-site breach.
detail: Reuters' framing comes from CNN's report, so it counts once.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: CNN calls it 'the second such breach in recent months' and names the September jobs-site attack.

claim_text: The NCIC intrusion is linked to this week's FAA, NSA, Microsoft 365 or Apple outages
summary: No source links them. CNN mentions the week's outages only as background and does not say they are connected.
detail: Officials have said the week's outages were not a cyberattack, but that was said before the NCIC report and does not mention NCIC.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: CNN and Reuters mention the outages as context only; neither reports a connection.

claim_text: On Nov 18, the White House said the week's tech outages were not a cyberattack
summary: A White House release quotes DNI Clayton: 'This is not a cyberattack,' and Secretary Rubio saying there is 'zero evidence' the incidents involved hackers or any malign actor.
detail: The release came out on Nov 18, before officials reportedly learned of the NCIC intrusion, and it does not mention NCIC or the FBI.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The White House release quotes both officials on the recent outages; it is dated Nov 18 and does not mention NCIC.

claim_text: The NCIC intrusion is linked to the September jobs-site breach or to ShinyHunters
summary: No source says the two FBI incidents are connected or that the same group is behind both.
detail: CNN reports them side by side only as a pattern of FBI breaches.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: CNN and NBC News describe the September breach as prior context and do not connect it; BleepingComputer says there is no indication the NCIC incident is connected to ShinyHunters or the earlier breach.

claim_text: the President spoke about the reported NCIC hack on Nov 21 but gave no details
summary: In a Fox News phone interview on Saturday, Nov 21, the President said of the reports: 'Well, we just heard about it, and I will say that it's not good. I don't like that.'
detail: He did not say what was reached, how, or by whom, and did not confirm the details of the reports. He suggested, without evidence, that the hack might surface information about past investigations; ABC News notes NCIC would not hold information on those investigations. The White House had not commented separately.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: ABC News, The Hill and Axios each quote the same remark from the Fox News interview. The Hill says he did not confirm the reports.
notes: Confirms that the President commented, not that NCIC was hacked. Read as a reaction to the reports, not an official confirmation.
